chapter_title: The Long Night Singing Its Dirges
title: Grace of the Goblet
subtitle: That affection, that greatness—it will eventually shine eternal.

items.text: Grace of the Goblet

items.speaker: George
items.text: My Lady, do we really have to do this?
George looked around nervously, clutching a delicate glass bottle tightly, the crimson liquid swaying inside.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: The monks themselves told me, moderate drinking is allowed.

items.speaker: George
items.text: And to make him blind drunk, is that considered moderate...?

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: That interpretation isn't up to you.

items.speaker: George
items.text: Well, just in case...

items.speaker: George
items.text: Ah, I see!
George slipped into the room, bathed in the gentle light of stained-glass windows.
The faithful had long finished their prayers and left.
George slowly approached, bowing in front of the priest's altar.

items.speaker: George
items.text: Father, I've come to seek the Lord's forgiveness.

items.speaker: George
items.text: I am a sinner, Father.

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: You've come late, George... and empty-handed. Confess then, and our merciful Lord will forgive your sins.
The priest looked down at the penitent believer, a veneer of kindness on his face marred by hungry eyes.
Then, he coughed twice.

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: Have you paid your tithes, George. Where are our cattle, our lambs? Did you bring them hence?

items.speaker: George
items.text: I did not, forgive me, Father... I need all that I have left for winter.
The merciful smile faded a second as the priest leaned out of the light.

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: No matter, George, your family comes first. But then have you some golden grain that might feed our faithful?

items.speaker: George
items.text: No, not that either, Father. I sold all that I had to spare at market...
The priest's kindness vanished into a gritted smile.

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text:
It seems you haven't truly repented yet...
Have you no concern for those who pray for you? Did you forget that the treasure shared with us in life, are stored doubly in heaven?

items.speaker: George
items.text: Forgive me then, father. That I only brought one such treasure with me.
George lifted his robe, revealing the top of a glass bottle.

items.speaker: George
items.text: That you might not forget me in your prayers, I beg you take it...
The warm light of mercy returned to the priest's face, and he opened his hand.

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: Ah!

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: A delightful smell, surely as pure as the wine at Cana, of course, I will save it to share in a time of celebration.

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: At last, I feel the sincerity of your repentance.

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: Go now; your sins have been forgiven.

items.speaker: George
items.text: Thank you, Father Malachi.
"Pop—"
The sound of the cork echoed against the empty chamber, hidden from the eyes of the stained-glass saints.
Father Malachi reeked of alcohol, he stumbled through the empty corridor, collapsing in front of the gaze of a statue.
His steps were unsteady, and he hadn't noticed Dikke standing in the shadows.

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: Oh Lord! Forgive me...

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: Burp—

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: I had only a little drink...

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: I'm not drunk... I didn't...

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Devoted as ever, Father Malachi.
Seizing the perfect moment, Dikke leaned against the angel statue, brandishing her flaming sword.
It gleamed like the blazing sun, with fierce fiery tongues dancing below the feet of the angel.

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: How... how are you here?

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: While you sought forgiveness through prayer, I sought the truth.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: And I've found it.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Brother Chester wasn't the only one fallen to drunkenness, it seems, or am I mistaken?

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: That poor wretch ... It wasn't me who did it. I swear ...

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: It was accidental! It was... I did not intend for him to fall ...

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Of course, your drinking together that night was nothing more than an act of camaraderie.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: You share your labors, your prayers, your wine, and it seems to me you even share corpses.
Dikke's shadow approached closer.

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: Never ... I had nothing to do with those corpses!

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: But if I hadn't discovered his wickedness, the abbot would never have permitted us to ostracize him...

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: He, he's lower than a carrion worm... ripe with the nauseating odor of a wizard!

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: Go down to the basement and see with your own eyes. It'll prove what I said is true... I've done nothing wrong!

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: For your sake, I hope so.
He leaned against the statue, his gaze wandering.

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: The great plague has been gone a long time...

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: As long as we do not intervene, people will forget those horrible events, and they will continue to believe in us...

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: ... Was that his crime?

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: A wizard trying to study corpses, awakening the painful memories of the people?

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: It is the truth! Given enough time, we will regain the trust of the people and their donations...

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: But, you see...

items.speaker: Malachi
items.text: Forgive me... Merciful Lord...
Malachi's ramblings stirred with the alcohol on his breath, creating a swamp of stench and confusion.
It was as if he didn't even realize what he was saying; muttering to himself until he collapsed on the ground.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Maybe your prayers will be heard.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Maybe your sins will be forgiven.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: But not right now, Father.
TO BE CONTINUED…
